bug.title: Following the margin's "Appeal" link, the post lands near the top and then drifts down to the lower part of the screen, and keeps a focus ring after a mouse click
bug.symptoms: discussion-tab.tsx (round 31, 03ec6d6) scrolls to #post-<cid> once when the threads are ready (~130 ms after load, against the signed-out layout) and focuses the post. The signed-in re-read then makes posts above it taller (234 px), and nothing re-aligns, so the post ends at 706 of 900 px (574 of 768 at 1366x768); a reply target drifts from 72 to 150 px. After a mouse click on the link the post keeps a 2 px focus ring until the reader clicks elsewhere. Evidence: 07-flag-and-dispute/80-r31-08a, 08e
bug.reproduction_steps: As sam, in the margin of his hidden annotation, click "Appeal"; watch the post's position for 2 s
bug.expected: Per D1/D2: after the first jump, while the same hash is current and the reader has not scrolled (wheel, touch, keys, scrollbar), typed or clicked, a later change of the threads (a re-read for the viewer) re-aligns the target once more with the same scrollIntoView({block: "start"}) honouring the card's scroll margin; after any reader input nothing moves them. The target gets a data-targeted (or :target) highlight from paper-discussion.css (design tokens only, a subtle accent edge or background that fades after ~2 s with prefers-reduced-motion respected), focus moves with preventScroll, and the card's focus outline appears only under :focus-visible (no ring after a mouse click on the link). Tests in discussion-tab.test.tsx: a re-render with taller content above re-aligns once; after a simulated wheel/keydown it does not; the highlight attribute is set on the target; the stylesheet's outline rule for the card is under :focus-visible
bug.actual: The post drifts away from where the reader was taken, with a stray focus ring

bug.title: The threads read that carries a member's own hidden post texts is sent without Cache-Control, unlike the annotations read in the same case
bug.symptoms: discussion/router.py get_threads (~L100-112) returns service.threads_for(..., viewer_did=...) with no cache header; for the author it includes own_text of their hidden posts (discussion/service.py ~L713-725). The annotations read (round 30, f1fba4c) sends Cache-Control: private, no-store when it carries own text. Seen in the sweep-24e re-check (diagnostic of sam's threads response)
bug.reproduction_steps: As sam (with hidden posts on sch:a4gc-nxee-pqsr), GET /v1/papers/sch:a4gc-nxee-pqsr/threads with his token; inspect the response headers
bug.expected: Per D3: whenever the threads read is made by a signed-in viewer (the answer may carry own_text and viewer-specific muting), the response has Cache-Control: private, no-store; an anonymous read keeps today's headers. Tests in test_hidden_posts.py: author's read → private, no-store and own_text present; anonymous read → no own_text and no private/no-store requirement change
bug.actual: A member's own hidden text can be kept by a browser cache
